brief: Goldman's Tony Pasquariello frames the tape as a cat-and-mouse game between equities and rates: the S&P held ~7,700 for two months, broke out Tuesday, then reversed back to 7,700 as yields gapped higher, and he blames the failed breakout on that rate move. His stated play: if carrying significant equity length, pair it with a simple trading short in bonds. Agentic AI (Meta's Muse) is doing the heavy lifting at the top of the cap stack; Rich Privorotsky calls it the first of many productivity-boosting entrants and sees the aggregate effect as bullish for equities and disinflationary, even as Goldman's own strategy desk notes AI-infrastructure valuations have already de-rated from 32x to 22x forward earnings on partly-priced skepticism. Small caps are underperforming for six weeks, sold by long-only funds and the wealth channel, which Pasquariello attributes mainly to the rate-driven tightening in financial conditions; he says he is not drawn to the trade now. Positioning is defensive (speculative length +3 of -10/+10) despite the market flirting with highs; buybacks are slowing and issuance is rising, though a genuine breakout could force fast money to chase quickly.
